facts.text: A hold-out set is test data reserved and never used for tuning; a tuning split divides data into tuning, confirmation and audit parts; cross-validation rotates the held-out part so every part is used for checking once.
facts.quote: A hold-out set is a portion of the test data kept back and never used for tuning, a tuning split is the division of data into parts for tuning, confirming and auditing, and cross-validation is the practice of rotating which part is held out so that every part is used for checking once.

facts.text: The booklet uses a three-way tuning split, with the tuning set used to adjust thresholds, zones and filters.
facts.quote: Tuning set: adjust thresholds, zones and filters

facts.text: The validation or confirmation set checks chosen settings on data not seen during tuning and may be consulted many times.
facts.quote: The validation or confirmation set checks the chosen settings on data the tuning did not see and may be looked at many times.

facts.text: The audit set, also called the frozen test set, remains untouched until the release candidate, is queried rarely, and is the only basis for the release claim.
facts.quote: The audit set, also called the frozen test set, is untouched until the release candidate, queried rarely, and is the only basis for the release claim.

facts.text: The audit set in the booklet's three-way split is pre-registered.
facts.quote: Audit set: frozen, pre-registered, queried only at release candidates

facts.text: The tuning, confirmation and audit partitions must be grouped rather than random: whole sites, weather episodes, machine identities or scenario families belong to one partition or another.
facts.quote: The parts must be grouped, not random: whole sites, weather episodes, machine identities or scenario families go into one part or another [Chapter 9].

facts.text: In the booklet's five-group cross-validation example, the system is tuned on four groups and checked on the fifth, repeated five times, and the checks are averaged.
facts.quote: Cross-validation rotates the role: with five groups, the system is tuned on four and checked on the fifth, five times over, and the checks are averaged.

facts.text: The booklet uses leave-one-site-type-out cross-validation for job sites.
facts.quote: "Leave-one-site-type-out" is the booklet's version for job sites.

facts.text: Nested cross-validation validates the choice of method inside the loop and is the recognized way to remove optimistic bias from repeated model selection in machine learning.
facts.quote: Nested cross-validation, where the choice of method is itself validated inside the loop, is the recognized way to remove the optimistic bias of repeated model selection in machine learning

facts.text: The booklet calls its three-way tuning split the engineering equivalent of nested cross-validation.
facts.quote: the booklet calls the three-way split its engineering equivalent [Chapter 9].

facts.text: In the three-way split, candidate settings move from tuning to confirmation and only then to the frozen audit set; the audit set never feeds back into tuning.
facts.quote: settings move from tuning to confirmation and only then to the frozen audit set, which never feeds back into tuning.

facts.text: The reusable holdout principle cited by the booklet allows the tuning team to see only aggregate pass or fail results from the audit set.
facts.quote: The "reusable holdout" principle the booklet cites means the tuning team sees only aggregate pass or fail from the audit set.

facts.text: When a failing audit case is examined and a threshold is changed in response, that audit case is contaminated and should be retired and replaced.
facts.quote: Whenever a failing audit case is examined and a threshold changed in response, that case is contaminated and should be retired and replaced [Chapter 9].
